pages.ko: 옛날 옛날 아주 먼 옛날에, 넓은 강가 마을에 마음씨 착한 할아버지와 할머니가 살았어요. 식구라고는 복슬복슬한 누렁이 복슬이와, 얌전한 고양이 나비뿐이었지요. 가난했지만 밥 한 술도 나누어 먹는 정다운 집이었답니다.
pages.t: Long, long ago, in a village beside a wide river, there lived a kind old grandfather and grandmother. Their whole family was one shaggy yellow dog named Bokseuri and one quiet cat named Nabi. They were poor, but it was a warm home where even a single spoonful of rice was shared.

pages.ko: 그날도 할아버지는 강가에 통발을 놓았어요. 텀벙— 건져 올리니 커다란 잉어 한 마리가 파닥파닥! 그런데 잉어의 눈이 그렁그렁 젖어 있지 뭐예요. "어이구, 가엾어라. 어서 가거라." 할아버지는 잉어를 강물에 살며시 놓아주었지요.
pages.t: That day, Grandfather set his woven fish trap in the river. Sploosh — when he lifted it out, a great big carp was flapping about inside! But look — the carp's eyes were brimming with tears. "Oh, you poor thing. Off you go now." And Grandfather slipped the carp gently back into the river.

pages.ko: 그날 밤이었어요. 찰랑— 강물이 갈라지더니, 낮에 놓아준 잉어가 쑤욱 올라왔지 뭐예요. "저는 용왕님의 아들이랍니다. 살려 주셔서 고맙습니다." 잉어는 반짝이는 구슬 한 알을 톡 내밀었어요. "소원을 말하면 무엇이든 나온답니다."
pages.t: That very night, the river went ripple— and parted, and up came the carp he had set free that afternoon! "I am the Dragon King's son. Thank you for saving my life." The carp held out one shining bead. "Say a wish, and anything at all will come out of it."

pages.ko: "따끈한 밥 한 상이 나와라!" 하니, 정말로 김이 모락모락 밥상이 차려졌어요! 할머니는 대바구니 가득 떡을 담아 이웃집에도 돌렸지요. 복슬이와 나비도 배가 통통, 마당은 하루 종일 웃음소리로 넉넉했답니다.
pages.t: "Let a table of warm rice appear!" — and truly, a steaming meal was laid out before them! Grandmother filled a big bamboo basket with rice cakes and passed them round to all the neighbors. Bokseuri and Nabi got nice round tummies too, and all day long the yard was full of laughter.

pages.ko: 강 건너 마을에는 욕심쟁이 영감이 살았어요. 소문을 듣고 슬금슬금 찾아와, 두리번두리번 방 안을 살폈지요. 그러고는 할아버지가 잠든 사이 구슬을 쏙— 소매에 넣고, 나룻배에 올라 삿대를 쭈욱 밀어 강을 건너가 버렸답니다.
pages.t: Across the river lived a greedy old man. When he heard the news he came sneaking over, peering this way and that around the room. Then, while Grandfather was fast asleep, he slipped the bead — whisk! — into his sleeve, climbed into a ferry boat, gave one long push with his pole, and crossed the river away.

pages.ko: 이튿날 아침, 구슬이 없어진 걸 안 할아버지와 할머니는 시무룩— 어깨가 축 처졌어요. 마루 밑에서 그 모습을 보던 복슬이와 나비는 서로 마주 보았지요. "우리가 찾아오자!" "그래, 함께 가자!"
pages.t: The next morning, when Grandfather and Grandmother saw that the bead was gone, their shoulders drooped down, down, down. Watching from under the wooden porch, Bokseuri and Nabi looked at each other. "Let's go and get it back!" "Yes — let's go together!"

pages.ko: 강물은 넓고 또 넓었어요. 복슬이는 첨벙첨벙 잘도 헤엄쳤지만, 나비는 물이 무서워 발끝만 콩콩. "내 등에 타!" 나비는 폴짝, 복슬이 등에 올라탔지요. "첨벙첨벙 건너가자! 꼭 붙잡았니?" "붙잡았지!"
pages.t: The river was wide, so very wide. Bokseuri swam splendidly, splish splash, but Nabi was afraid of the water and only tapped it with her toes. "Climb on my back!" Hop! Nabi jumped up onto Bokseuri's back. "Splish splash, across we go! Are you holding on tight?" "I'm holding on!"

pages.ko: 욕심쟁이 영감네 곳간은 캄캄했어요. 그때 구석에서 찍찍— 생쥐 한 마리가 쪼르르 나왔지요. 나비가 눈을 반짝이며 말했어요. "구슬을 찾아 주면, 오늘은 못 본 척해 줄게!" 생쥐는 고개를 끄덕끄덕했답니다.
pages.t: Inside the greedy old man's storeroom it was pitch dark. Then, from a corner — squeak, squeak! — out scurried a little mouse. Nabi's eyes shone. "Find the bead for me, and I'll pretend I never saw you today!" The mouse nodded and nodded.

pages.ko: 생쥐는 나무 궤짝 밑으로 쏙 들어가 사각사각 구멍을 냈어요. 잠시 뒤, 데구루루— 반짝이는 구슬이 굴러 나왔지 뭐예요! 나비는 구슬을 입에 꼭 물었어요. "고마워, 생쥐야!"
pages.t: The mouse slipped under the wooden chest and gnawed a hole, scritch scratch. A moment later — roll, roll, roll — out came the shining bead! Nabi held the bead tight in her mouth. "Thank you, little mouse!"

pages.ko: 돌아오는 길, 나비는 다시 복슬이 등에 폴짝 올라탔어요. 복슬이는 신이 나서 노래하듯 물었지요. "첨벙첨벙 건너가자! 물었니?" "으응—!" "놓쳤니?" "으응!" 입을 꼭 다문 채 웅얼웅얼. 그건 "물었지!" "아니야!" 라는 뜻이었지요.
pages.t: On the way home, Nabi hopped up onto Bokseuri's back again. Bokseuri was so happy that he asked in a singsong voice, "Splish splash, across we go! Have you got it?" "Mm-hmm—!" "Did you drop it?" "Mm-hmm!" She mumbled with her mouth clamped shut. What she meant was "I've got it!" and "I did not!"

pages.ko: 그런데 복슬이가 자꾸자꾸 물었어요. "정말 물었니? 진짜로 물었니?" 답답해진 나비가 "물었다니까—!" 하고 입을 벌린 순간, 퐁당! 구슬이 물속으로 쏙 빠져 버렸어요. "네가 자꾸 물어봤잖아!" "네가 입을 벌렸잖아!" 둘은 홱— 서로 고개를 돌려 버렸지요.
pages.t: But Bokseuri kept asking and asking. "Have you really got it? Have you truly got it?" Nabi grew so cross that she opened her mouth — "I said I've GOT it—!" — and plop! The bead dropped straight down into the water. "You kept asking me!" "You opened your mouth!" And the two of them turned their heads away with a huff.

pages.ko: 복슬이는 삐친 채로도 나비를 강가까지 태워다 주고는, 뒤도 안 돌아보고 먼저 집으로 가 버렸어요. 나비는 강가를 서성서성… 그때 물결이 찰랑, 낯익은 잉어가 쑤욱 올라왔지 뭐예요. 잉어의 입에는 반짝이는 구슬이 물려 있었지요. "이건 착한 마음에게 드린 거예요. 어서 가져가세요."
pages.t: Even sulking, Bokseuri carried Nabi all the way to the riverbank, then trotted home first without looking back once. Nabi paced up and down the shore… and then the water went ripple, and up came a familiar carp! There in the carp's mouth was the shining bead. "This is a gift for a kind heart. Take it home quickly."

pages.ko: 나비는 구슬을 물고 한달음에 집으로 달려왔어요. "아이고, 우리 나비!" 할머니는 나비를 폭 안아 주었지요. 마루 밑에서 복슬이가 코를 씰룩였어요. 그러자 할아버지가 복슬이의 등도 쓱쓱 쓰다듬어 주었답니다. "복슬이도 참 애썼구나."
pages.t: Nabi carried the bead in her mouth and ran all the way home in one dash. "Oh my goodness, our Nabi!" Grandmother scooped her up in a great big hug. Under the porch, Bokseuri twitched his nose. So Grandfather stroked Bokseuri's back too. "Bokseuri worked very hard as well."

pages.ko: 그날 저녁, 마당은 다시 웃음으로 넉넉했어요. 그런데 복슬이와 나비는요? 마주칠 때마다 고개를 홱— 서로 데면데면했지 뭐예요. "물었니?" "…" 그래서 지금도 개와 고양이는 만나면 슬쩍 눈을 흘긴대요. 함께 해낸 일은 함께 기뻐해야 오래오래 사이좋게 지낼 수 있대요.
pages.t: That evening the yard was full of laughter again. But what about Bokseuri and Nabi? Every time they met, they turned their heads away — huff! — and would not say a word to each other. "Have you got it?" "…" And that is why, even today, dogs and cats give each other a sideways look when they meet. When you do something together, they say, you must be happy about it together too — that is how you stay friends for a long, long time.
